rv.q: Billy Crystal’s new one-man show, 860 , is a love story. The 78 year old comedian has a lot of love in his life: his wife Janice to whom he’s been married for 56 years, his two daughters, Jenny and Lindsay, and his grandsons.

Crystal, still remarkably spry and vibrant at age 78, delivers the show from a set designed by Scott Pask recreating his home office filled with a lifetime’s worth of memorabilia including numerous Emmy Awards, signed photographs, and even a wooden seat from the original Yankee Stadium.
If you make anything drawn from your own life, 860 is a masterclass in turning private loss into something an audience can hold.

sg.ra: Closest and most direct view of the stage at Imperial Theatre, with the fullest sound. The standard top pick for any show here.
An elevated, full-stage view with no orchestra-level neck-craning — especially strong for shows with big staging or choreography.
A modest side angle on the stage but still close and clear — a reliable choice when center seats are sold out.
Farther from the stage than center orchestra — less up-close, but the sound still carries well.
A noticeable side angle, but Imperial Theatre's more moderate size keeps the distance from the stage manageable.

vs.sum: The Imperial Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions and solid sound quality, though some seats may miss minor stage action. While the ambiance is enhanced by its historic architectural design, comfort is average with decent legroom. Facilities are lacking, with long restroom lines being a common issue.

acc.note: 5 wheelchair locations in Orchestra. No steps from sidewalk. Infrared devices available.
